title: Alternatives to Built
summary: A short, objective look at alternatives to Built for construction lenders, including Rabbet, Land Gorilla, and Abrigo, with guidance on choosing by loan type and institution.
body_markdown:
If you are a construction lender looking at Built, it helps to see the other platforms that handle construction loan administration and where each one fits. This guide gives a short, objective rundown of the alternatives lenders most often consider.


## What Built is


Built is a construction loan management software that handles draw administration, inspection management, lien waiver and compliance tracking for construction lenders.


## Popular alternatives


### Rabbet for Construction Lenders


Rabbet for Construction Lenders is a finance system that covers draw review, budgets, compliance, and portfolio insights. Rabbet brings budgets, documents, and draw activity into one organized loan administration system, with automated checks built in so standards hold as the portfolio scales, and portfolio views that surface budget changes and exposure early. It is commonly considered by banks, credit unions, regional and warehouse lenders, private lenders, and private credit firms.


### Land Gorilla


Construction loan management software with a bundled inspection service. Land Gorilla is residential-focused and pairs draw management with a turnkey inspector network, which makes it a fit for residential lenders that want inspections managed for them.


### Abrigo


Lending, compliance, and risk software oriented to community institutions. Abrigo is commonly considered by community banks and credit unions that already use it for origination or compliance and want to keep more of that work with one vendor.


## How to choose


The best fit comes down to a few questions: the loan types you make, the systems you already run, and how your team needs to report. Residential-heavy books value a bundled inspection network. Community institutions often weigh what already sits in their existing stack. Lenders that run a mix of commercial, residential, and homebuilder lines, and that want portfolio control as volume grows, tend to prioritize a platform that brings budgets, documents, draws, and reporting into one place.


For a deeper breakdown by lender type, loan type, and team size, see our guide to the best construction loan management software for lenders.
